newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens weaker on Bre-X drill results.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens weaker on Bre-X drill results.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar opened slightly weaker in light trading on Monday at C$1.3825 (US$0.7233) after testing the C$1.3783 (US$0.7255) level overnight in Asian markets, traders said. * They said the currency was hit after an independent analysis of drill results from the Bre-X Minerals Ltd Busang mine in Indonesia found insignificant amounts of gold.
"We got to C$1.3783 (US$0.7255) in Singapore, and then it sold off on the Bre-X story," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy.
But Farrill said the damage had already been done to the Canada dollar and expected little further downswing as a result of the scandal.
"There should be some impact, but I don't think it's going to be profound. It's not really a Canada dollar story," Farrill said.
Traders expected the dollar to trade in a narrow range today with no U.S. economic data due to be released.
Markets in London and Tokyo are closed for holidays today, which also will take some of the momentum out of the dollar's recent rise, traders said.
"The Canadian dollar would appear to be set for a week of consolidation," one trader said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar slid to 1.2507 marks from Friday's close of 1.2520 and fell to 91.47 yen from 91.57 yen.
